currentFormal: breadth>=40 && avgChange>=-1 && amountVs20DayAverage>=0.5, with nonfinite breadth/avgChange rejected
findings: The three gate inputs do not share one denominator.
breadth denominator is every industry todayRow; (changePercent||0)>0 means missing/NaN change is treated as non-advance.
avgChange denominator is only finite changePercent rows; average of an empty finite set returns 0.
amountVs20DayAverage denominator/numerator use only rows whose matched feature has historyDays>=20.

The activity subset does not separately require avgAmount20 to be observed/positive before membership; missing avgAmount20 contributes 0 to the denominator while tradeValue can still contribute to the numerator.
All three deployed sector statistics include the candidate itself; sectorReturn20 earlier in the pipeline is different and explicitly excludes the candidate from its peer return average.
Old PR #111 preserves final gate values/pass state but not the mixed denominator counts, missingness composition or candidate self-contribution needed for a promotion-grade falsification.

fixedCounterexamples.interpretation: Self inclusion can mechanically alter current gate state. This does not prove leave-one-out is superior.

fixedCounterexamples.consequence: A history-ready row with missing avgAmount20 can add current tradeValue without adding baseline amount, inflating the activity ratio.
